subject: Permissioned egress journey: allowlist, proxy, and firewall checklist for private endpoints
body:
From: Samir Patel <infra@meditech.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Permissioned egress: initial questions for private endpoint deployment

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week. We're starting the security review for Redwood Private (VPC) and need a clear, prescriptive list of outbound connectivity requirements for your private endpoint deployment. Specific asks from our infra and security teams:

- Minimal IP ranges (CIDRs) and per-service ports that must be NATed/allowlisted on our egress firewall
- Whether Redwood requires direct outbound access to public S3 endpoints, or if it can be routed through a customer-owned proxy (we'd prefer proxying for audit)
- TLS expectations (mutual TLS to control plane? SNI-only?) and which hostnames must resolve externally vs. be split-horizon
- DNS, CRL/OCSP, and KMS endpoints that must be reachable
- Any hard dependency on third-party CDNs or observability endpoints that will originate from your runtime
- Suggested logging/packet capture points for later audits

We're trying to avoid overly permissive 0.0.0.0/0 egress rules. Can you provide an actionable checklist we can drop into our change request?

Thanks,
Samir
InfraOps — Meditech Health

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: Samir Patel <infra@meditech.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Permissioned egress: allowlist, proxy, and firewall checklist for private endpoints

Samir — appreciate the clear breakdown. Looping in Laura (network) and Marissa (solutions) to provide concrete IP lists and an ops-friendly checklist. High level answers:

- We support both direct outbound (to AWS/GCP/Azure endpoints) and customer-owned egress proxies. For regulated customers we commonly recommend routing all outbound through a corporate proxy or NAT gateway under the customer's control.
- Control plane interactions (account provisioning, metrics upload, console) can be configured to use mutual TLS when deployed private; however, the runtime nodes also need to reach a small, permissioned set of addresses for model artifacts and dependency resolution.
- DNS split-horizon is supported and often used: internal hostnames (e.g., model-registry.internal) should resolve to your private hosts, while public cert validation/OCSP often requires outbound access to public CA infrastructure.

Laura/Marissa — can you add an itemized checklist with CIDRs, ports, and recommended proxy headers (we use X-Forwarded-* + mTLS client cert option)? Also note any ephemeral port ranges for streaming and KV cache sync.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

---
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: Samir Patel <infra@meditech.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Permissioned egress: allowlist, proxy, and firewall checklist for private endpoints

Samir / Team — attaching a pragmatic checklist and the minimal IP set we ask customers to allow (attached as redwood-egress-ipset.csv). I'll summarize the essentials inline so you can copy into a change ticket.

1) Principled approach- Keep outbound policies permissioned (deny by default) and explicitly allow: control plane endpoints, artifact storage, key management, and telemetry endpoints. Use a customer-managed proxy/NAT if you require centralized audit/logging.

2) Minimal outbound endpoints (examples; CIDRs are maintained in CSV attachment):
- Redwood control plane API: 34.210.12.0/24, 34.210.13.0/24 (HTTPS 443) — used for account operations, rollouts, and console UI. If you prefer proxy-only, route these through your proxy with pass-through TLS.
- Model artifact store (S3-equivalent): 52.216.0.0/20 (HTTPS 443) — runtime downloads model weight blobs and subgraph artifacts during cold starts; allow to either public S3 or a VPC endpoint.
- Public model registry metadata (CDN): 3.5.0.0/22 (HTTPS 443) — small GET/HEAD traffic for manifest files.
- Metrics/telemetry ingestion (optional; can be disabled): 13.35.0.0/24 (UDP/TCP 443) — we can also tunnel telemetry via your proxy or send to a customer-managed telemetry sink.

3) Ports and protocols- HTTPS (443) required for all control and artifact endpoints. Streaming responses use long-lived TLS connections; ephemeral high ports on the client side are expected but outbound destination port stays 443. If you block ephemeral outbound ranges, ensure TCP NAT table supports many concurrent ephemeral sockets.

4) Proxying recommendations- If using a corporate proxy:
- Allow CONNECT to destinations on port 443 and preserve SNI (unless you perform TLS interception).
- Preferred: configure proxy to allow mTLS for the Redwood client cert if you require client authentication.
- Add X-Remote-User / X-Forwarded-For headers for audit correlation (we respect them for logging).

5) DNS and certificate checks- Ensure your environment allows outbound to public CA OCSP/CRL endpoints (usually ephemeral HTTPs calls) or alternatively integrate with your internal OCSP responder. DNS split-horizon recommended for private artifact endpoints; validate that resolvers can answer both internal and public records where appropriate.

6) KMS and secrets endpoints- If using customer KMS, open outbound to your KMS control plane endpoints (region-specific). For Redwood-managed KMS interactions (optional), the typical endpoints are 52.219.100.0/24 (HTTPS 443).

7) Observability and audit- Allow egress for syslog/forwarder IPs if you want real-time packet logs. For periodic evidence collection we provide a signed manifest and S3 access logs — no continuous 0.0.0.0/0 egress required.

8) Hardening & operational notes-
- Use NAT IP rotation if your change window requires ephemeral CIDR swaps; inform Redwood for coordination.
- Keep a short-lived allowlist during onboarding and narrow it after heat map validation.
- For failover, Redwood can fallback to a secondary region; please allow the secondary control plane CIDRs in a canary policy.

Attachments: redwood-egress-ipset.csv (columns: service, cidr, port, protocol, notes) and meditech-egress-requirements.xlsx (your internal template).

If you want, we can produce a permutation of this checklist that maps directly into your change ticket fields (we've done that for other customers).

--
Laura Bennett
Network Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0127

Samir — following up to confirm next steps and owners:

- Meditech infra will ingest redwood-egress-ipset.csv into your change request (Samir) — target: schedule maintenance window 2026-09-24
- Meditech Security will confirm whether you will intercept TLS (MITM) or accept end-to-end mTLS from the runtime (Megan) — action: choose by 2026-09-20
- Redwood (Laura) will provide a secondary control-plane CIDR and a canary rollout plan after you confirm the maintenance window
- Redwood (Marissa) will produce a ticket-ready checklist mapping to your change request fields and provide a sample proxy config for Squid/Nginx (by 2026-09-17)

Quick clarifications for your change ticket copy-paste:
- Primary allowlist: control plane 34.210.12.0/24, 34.210.13.0/24; artifact store 52.216.0.0/20; registry CDN 3.5.0.0/22. Destination port: 443 only.
- If routing through your proxy: allow CONNECT to destination:443; preserve SNI and pass X-Forwarded headers.
- DNS: allow public CA OCSP endpoints or provide OCSP responder details.

I'll join the change review call if helpful. Thanks again — happy to run a dry-run validation with your infra team the week of the maintenance window.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
